rows: An octopus resolves about 3 to 12 cycles per degree, and a cuttlefish about 8. A squid resolves about 0.6, so the screen is blurred to what the animal would keep. The picture uses a middle value of 6.
Most records say the group has one visual pigment and sees no colour. The picture is therefore drawn in one brightness channel, with only a little colour left.
An octopus or squid sees about 180 degrees on one side, and a squid of 7 days old sees about 311 degrees. The picture uses a wide field of 180 degrees.

The soft edges, the shallow focus, the slit pupil, the brightness channel and the lack of sheen are the app's own choices, set inside the measured ranges. Polarised light is not drawn, because no engine setting carries it.
The sharp middle and the soft edge of the picture are the app's guess, since the records describe a central streak in the retina but give no sharpness across the field.

claims.how: The value 6 lies between the squid record of 0.63 cycles per degree and the octopus record of 12.23, and the cuttlefish record of 8 sits inside that span.
The value 180 equals the wider-group figure of roughly 180 degrees on one side of the animal.
